patch.value: The search and MCP content-enrichment paths consume URLs returned by a configured SearXNG instance. Trusted-domain scoring currently uses raw substring matching, so an unrelated hostname can embed a trusted token. Remote content fetching accepts arbitrary URL schemes and buffers the entire response before truncating extracted text. Implement hostname-aware trust rules, reject unsupported or local URL targets, validate redirects, restrict content types, and cap downloaded bytes before parsing.
Harden remote content fetching and URL trust scoring
Prevent attacker-controlled URLs from receiving trusted-domain relevance bonuses and bound remote content retrieval to safe web schemes and finite response sizes.

A URL containing github.com outside its hostname receives no trust bonus; only HTTP(S) remote targets are fetched; loopback/private literal targets and credential-bearing URLs are rejected; redirect targets are revalidated; unsupported content types and oversized responses are not buffered; regression tests cover each boundary
Concrete vulnerable call sites and existing unit-test locations are identified.
CLI search enrichment and MCP search tool when fetchContent/fetch_content is enabled
Score https://evil.example/path/github.com with an unrelated title; or return a file/private/very-large URL from the configured SearXNG instance and request fetched content.
Trust bonuses depend on parsed hostname boundaries and content enrichment only performs bounded fetches to acceptable public web targets.
Raw URL substring matches grant trust and fetch() buffers response.text() without validating scheme, target class, redirect destination, content type, or response size.
A malicious or compromised search backend can distort ranking and induce resource-heavy or local-target fetch attempts from the CLI host.
